Netmizaaggamig Nishnaabeg

Netmizaaggamig Nishnaabeg identifies itself as an Anishinaabe community connected to White Lake and the White River travel route. Its public account explains its reclaimed name and distinction from other communities; a dated joint announcement supplies a separate record of reserve-land expansion.

These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

White Lake and a reclaimed name

The Nation’s own public account places White Lake at the centre of travel, food and community identity. It explains Netmizaaggamig as the first lake reached when paddling north from Lake Superior along the White River. The account says the Nation reclaimed its name in2021 after years of being called Pic Mobert, and explicitly distinguishes its history from a supposed single larger Pic Band. That distinction helps readers avoid conflating neighbouring First Nations.

Read the sources [1] Netmizaaggamig Nishnaabeg / Pic Mobert First Nation

02

A dated record of reserve expansion

A joint April2021 announcement links a completed Reserve North addition to a1992 framework and a2015 final agreement. It describes the process as a route outside the land-claim process for community development. Its quick facts separately identify a proposed Reserve South addition that still depended on requirements being satisfied. This dated record should not be collapsed into every later land transaction or treated as settling the Nation’s wider title position.

Read the sources [2] Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada

About Us: Our Nation and Reclaiming Our Name ↗

Selected public sections explain the community’s White Lake connection, an original reserve purchased by members in1922 and reclamation of its name in2021. The Nation explicitly rejects a conflation with a single larger Pic Band. Its statements of title and jurisdiction remain attributed positions, not legal findings by this directory.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Read Our Nation and Reclaiming Our Name in full, plus the surrounding headings to establish scope; no separate examination of linked constitution, archival paylist, photographs or detailed tenure account.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Netmizaaggamig Nishnaabeg (Pic Mobert First Nation), Canada and Ontario announce the completion of an Addition to Reserve process ↗

Publication: 2021-04-15

Read the April15,2021 joint announcement’s substantive body, Chief’s quotation and quick facts. It distinguishes a completed Reserve North addition from a then-conditional Reserve South process, and describes1992 and2015 agreements. It is a dated government/community announcement, not the agreements, a title judgment or proof that all planned development occurred.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete substantive release body, quotations and quick facts; linked policies, agreements, land plans and underlying transfer instruments not inspected.
